newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Notionnel vol flat ahead of public audit.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Notionnel vol flat ahead of public audit.

text.p: Implied volatility of front month notionnel options traded on MATIF was broadly stable on Thursday ahead of an audit report commissioned by the French government on the state of public finances due out on Monday, traders said.
"This audit story is pretty much in the market," said Henri-Pierre Boissieres, notionnel options trader at Paribas in Paris.
"We've seen some selling of the 131.00 calls but the market is pretty quiet."

France's new Socialist-led government commissioned an audit of public finances when it came to power, saying it wanted details of the state of the public purse before it decided on measures to curb the deficit.

The results of the study -- which will include a forecast of the total public deficit for this year -- are due to be presented to a closed-door hearing of the parliamentary finance committee at 0900 GMT on Monday.
Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn is also due to testify before the same committee at 1300 GMT.
Jonathan Morris, an options broker at Finacor, also noted the selling of the 131.00 strike calls in August. "But as you can see that hasn't paid off just yet because the spot rallied," he said.
By 1410 GMT, more than 4,500 lots of the contract had been traded, while September notionnel futures were up 0.30 at 130.44.
Traders said August mid-vol was at an unchanged 4.0 percent -- 4.10 percent at the 130.00 strike and 3.90 percent at the 131.00 strike.
They said September vol was also flat, at 4.40 percent.
Morris noted net sellers of puts on September on the downside. By mid afternoon over 4,000 lots of the 128.00 September put had been traded and over 1,600 at the 129.00 strike.
